meta.title: Three Word Groups in the Cooking Class

paragraphs: On Saturday, the Explorers went to the cooking class. Chef Lucy gave each child a white apron. The room smelled of sweet fruit, and the children were happy. Each table had a knife, a spoon, a fork, and a bowl. "Today we will make a fruit salad," she said. "We will also learn three groups of words." She wrote three words on the board: Fruit, Tools, and Hand.

"The first group is fruit," said Chef Lucy. "Strawberry, mango, banana, and apple are in this group." The children washed the fruit in cold water. Mia washed the apple and the banana. Lily cut a strawberry into two pieces. It was red and sweet, and it smelled wonderful. "Which fruit do you like best?" asked Chef Lucy. "I like mango," said Mia.

"The second group is tools," said Chef Lucy. "Knife, spoon, fork, and chopsticks are in this group." Leo took a pair of chopsticks to eat the salad. "Chopsticks are hard to use," he said. A piece of mango fell on the table. Chef Lucy showed him how to hold the chopsticks. Leo tried again, and he picked up a strawberry. He smiled and said thank you.

"The third group is the hand," said Chef Lucy. "Finger, thumb, and bandage are in this group." Mia was cutting an apple when the knife touched her finger. She had a small cut. Chef Lucy looked at it carefully. The cut was very small. Chef Lucy put a bandage on her finger. "You might cut your finger with a knife," she said. "So always cut away from your hand."

"Now you know three groups of words," said Chef Lucy. The Explorers ate the fruit salad together. Mia looked at her bandage and smiled. "My finger is fine," she said. Lily wrote the three groups for Explorers' Blog that night.
